options: A named reference to a file location that COPY INTO reads from — not a copy of the data itself
A temporary table that holds loaded rows before they're queryable
A snapshot of a table taken before every load
A Snowsight dashboard for monitoring warehouse usage
questions.explain: A stage is metadata pointing at a location — internal or external — plus remembered settings like file format and credentials; the file itself doesn't move until COPY INTO runs.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three kinds of internal stage?
options: Storage integration stage
User stage (@~)
Table stage (@%table_name)
Named internal stage
questions.explain: The three internal stage types are user, table, and named. A storage integration is a separate object (covered in Chapter 4) used to authorize external stages without hardcoded credentials.

questions.q: What does an external stage point at?
options: Cloud storage you already own — an S3, Azure Blob, or GCS bucket — without copying the files into Snowflake first
A stage inside another Snowflake account
A local folder on the user's laptop
A view defined on top of a table
questions.explain: External stages reference storage that already exists outside Snowflake, letting other tools keep using those same files.

questions.q: Why might a company with an existing S3 data lake default to external stages rather than internal ones?
options: Because other tools besides Snowflake still need to read those same raw files, so the data has to keep living in the lake
Because external stages are always faster to query than internal stages
Because Snowflake cannot create internal stages inside AWS accounts
Because internal stages require a paid add-on
questions.explain: When a data lake is shared across multiple systems, Snowflake stays one consumer of the existing files rather than becoming the sole owner by copying everything internally.

questions.q: In the lesson's CREATE STAGE examples, what does the internal stage need that the external stage doesn't require additionally?
options: Nothing extra — it's the external stage that needs more: a URL and credentials on top of a name
A warehouse size setting
A primary key definition
A Snowpipe subscription
questions.explain: A named internal stage can be created with just a name (and optional file format); an external stage additionally needs a URL pointing at the bucket and credentials (or a storage integration).
